featured.title: The US Just Blocked Foreigners From Anthropic's Best AI. Indian Engineers Are in the Crossfire.
featured.excerpt: Commerce Secretary Lutnick's export ban on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 hits Anthropic's foreign-born workforce, TCS's new Claude deployment, and every Indian company that was using these models to patch vulnerabilities.
featured.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at TechCrunch Disrupt
featured.nri_angle: Indian engineers at Anthropic are barred from using the models they helped build, TCS's 50,000-employee Claude deployment faces regulatory uncertainty, and Indian enterprise customers lose access to critical cybersecurity tools.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: From Memes to Monarchy: RCB's Dynasty Has Arrived
editorial.excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru retain the IPL title with a five-wicket demolition of Gujarat Titans in Ahmedabad — and a 15-year-old from Sambalpur might just have stolen the entire season.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Opendoor Just Shut Its Entire India Office and Replaced 250 Workers With AI. Silicon Valley Is Watching.
news.excerpt: The real estate tech firm's exit from Chennai and Bengaluru is being called a 'watershed moment' for India's offshoring industry — and TCS's own chairman says AI agents will soon match its workforce head for head.
news.image_caption: An empty call centre office with rows of desks and computers — the kind of workspace now being replaced by AI
news.nri_angle: For the millions of Indian IT professionals whose careers were built on the offshoring model, Opendoor's exit is a warning shot — and the restructuring of India's $315 billion IT sector will reshape job markets for NRIs and their families for years.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Peace Deal Could Be Signed This Weekend. India's Markets Just Had Their Best Day in Two Months.
news.excerpt: Brent crude fell to its lowest since March, the Sensex surged 2.3 per cent, and the rupee rallied to 95.11 — all on a deal that has not actually been signed yet.
news.image_caption: A stock market screen showing numbers and data — Indian benchmarks logged their best session in two months on Friday
news.nri_angle: For NRIs with Indian market investments, rupee-denominated assets, or family back home dealing with rising fuel and food costs, a peace deal could reverse months of damage — but the terms still favour Tehran.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's EV Market Grew 81 Per Cent Last Year. Tesla Sold 35 Cars Last Month.
news.excerpt: Tata doubled its electric car sales, Mahindra doubled too, Maruti entered with 1,591 units — and India just told Tesla it can either build a factory or keep its showrooms.
news.image_caption: A public electric vehicle charging station — India's EV infrastructure is racing to keep up with 80 per cent annual sales growth
news.nri_angle: For NRIs considering an EV for family in India or tracking the Indian market for investment, the numbers are clear — India's EV revolution is being built by homegrown brands, and Tesla is barely a footnote.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Preparing to Miss Its Budget Deficit Target for the First Time Since the Pandemic. The Iran War Is the Reason.
news.excerpt: Bloomberg reports the government will let the fiscal gap widen to 4.8% of GDP — half a percentage point above the February target — as energy subsidies balloon and oil stays above $85 a barrel.
news.image_caption: India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during a diplomatic meeting in Vienna, April 2025
news.nri_angle: A wider deficit weakens the rupee and raises the risk of sovereign credit downgrades, directly affecting NRI investments, remittance values, and the attractiveness of FCNR deposits that banks are now offering at up to 7%.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Meta Will Build Its First AI Data Centre in India. Reliance Will Run It From Ambani's Jamnagar Complex.
news.excerpt: The 168-megawatt facility — powered by renewable energy, cooled by desalinated seawater — marks the deepest infrastructure bet any American tech giant has made in India. Delivery is expected within two years.
news.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, Chairman of Reliance Industries, whose Jamnagar complex will house Meta's first Indian AI data centre
news.nri_angle: The Jamnagar facility signals India's evolution from talent source to core AI infrastructure hub, opening new career paths for Indian tech professionals while adding a major revenue stream to Reliance ahead of Jio Platforms' anticipated IPO.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Unveils Project Kusha, Its Homegrown Answer to Russia's S-400. Rajnath Singh Says It Already Proved Itself in Combat.
news.excerpt: The indigenous air defence system features three interceptor variants with ranges up to 400 km. The defence minister says Operation Sindoor settled the debate.
news.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at a government event in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: Project Kusha positions India as a potential exporter of advanced air defence technology, opening strategic consulting and defence-tech opportunities for the diaspora.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Sixty-Four of Eighty TMC Lawmakers Have Abandoned Mamata Banerjee. The Party She Built Is Splitting in Two.
news.excerpt: The rebel faction controls 78% of the legislature party and has installed its own Leader of the Opposition. The revolt targets Abhishek Banerjee, not his aunt.
news.image_caption: Mamata Banerjee at a public event in Kolkata
news.nri_angle: TMC was a cultural-political anchor for the Bengali diaspora globally; the split reshapes Bengal's economic trajectory and its diaspora networks' political affiliations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: South India Now Carries More Air Passengers Than the North and West Combined. The Gap Is Still Growing.
news.excerpt: Southern airports handled 41% of India's international traffic last year. IT hubs, Gulf routes, and GCC investments have redrawn the country's aviation map.
news.image_caption: Air India aircraft parked on the tarmac at an Indian airport
news.nri_angle: More international capacity through Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and Chennai means better direct routes and schedules for NRIs flying home to south India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi and Macron Will Unveil 120 Indian Deep-Tech Startups in Nice Tomorrow. Nothing Like This Has Happened Before.
news.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026, the first showcase of its kind, brings startups from IITs, IISc and BITS Pilani to 500 global investors across 13 sectors. Twenty-eight MoUs are expected on day one.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron at the India AI Impact Summit earlier this year
news.nri_angle: Indian-origin entrepreneurs and NRI investors in Europe can directly engage with India's deep-tech pipeline, while the MoUs could open research and commercialisation pathways for diaspora professionals in AI, biotech and semiconductors.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The World Bank Just Upgraded India While Downgrading Almost Everyone Else. The Gap Is Getting Wider.
news.excerpt: India is one of the only major economies to see its growth forecast raised in the June 2026 Global Economic Prospects report. The world is slowing to its weakest pace since COVID. India is not.
news.image_caption: The World Bank Group headquarters in Washington, D.C.
news.nri_angle: NRI investors weighing India allocation decisions get a clearer signal: India is the fastest-growing large economy, but the Iran war, El Nino risk and energy costs are real headwinds that affect remittance purchasing power and return-to-India timelines.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Ripped Up Its Tax Code for Foreign Bond Investors. A Billion Dollars Flowed In Within Three Days.
news.excerpt: The government scrapped withholding and capital gains taxes on foreign investments in government bonds — the most aggressive move to attract overseas capital since the crisis began. State Street calls it a 'game-changer.'
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: The same policy package that opened bonds to foreigners also incentivised NRI dollar deposits with RBI-backed hedging — part of a coordinated push to draw diaspora capital that directly affects NRI savings rates, rupee stability and remittance purchasing power.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: SBI and Bank of Baroda Are About to Borrow a Billion Dollars Abroad. The RBI Is Paying Part of Their Hedging Cost.
news.excerpt: The two state-run lenders will be the first to tap a subsidised swap window that bankers expect to pull in $15 to $20 billion over the next six months.
news.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes — the RBI is subsidising hedging costs to pull dollars into the country
news.nri_angle: NRI deposits are a key part of the RBI's dollar strategy — the central bank is also fully subsidising hedging costs on three-to-five-year foreign currency deposits raised from non-resident Indians, which SBI alone expects could bring in $34 billion.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: 136 Million Barrels of Oil Got Through the 'Closed' Strait of Hormuz. The Market Is Just Finding Out.
news.excerpt: Dark tankers, switched-off transponders and 'goat paths' along the Omani coastline kept crude flowing while the world watched the blockade. Oil has crashed to a two-month low.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker transits open waters — millions of barrels have moved through the Gulf via dark shipping routes
news.nri_angle: India is the world's third-largest oil importer and every dollar off the barrel saves billions on its import bill — the slide from $120 to below $86 has already eased pressure on the rupee, inflation and government finances.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Corporate Bond Market Just Had Its Biggest Week in Months. Borrowing Costs Fell 45 Basis Points in Five Days.
news.excerpt: Bajaj Finance, Muthoot, NABARD and a string of NBFCs are rushing to lock in cheap debt after the RBI's dollar measures triggered a sharp rally in short-term bonds.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai's Dalal Street financial district
news.nri_angle: Lower corporate borrowing costs ripple through the economy — from cheaper home loans to better returns on NRI fixed deposits — and signal that India's credit markets are absorbing the oil shock faster than feared.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: France Just Invited India to Every Session of the G7. No Guest Country Has Ever Got That Before.
news.excerpt: Modi will sit in on all six working sessions at Évian next week — a diplomatic first that says as much about France's ambitions as India's rise.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who will attend all six sessions of the G7 summit in France
news.nri_angle: The 1.1 million Indians in Europe stand to benefit from deeper India-France defence, tech and startup cooperation — and G7 discussions on AI governance will shape rules affecting Indian tech workers across the continent.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. The RBI Is Picking Up the Tab.
news.excerpt: A desperate play to defend the rupee has created the best NRI deposit rates in over a decade. The window closes in September.
news.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and banking instruments
news.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, UK, Canada and Gulf can earn 6-7% guaranteed returns on dollar deposits with zero exchange rate risk — the best rates in over a decade.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Musk Is Now Worth a Trillion Dollars. SpaceX Hit $2 Trillion on Day One. India Still Will Not Let It Turn On Starlink.
news.excerpt: The largest IPO in history minted the world's first trillionaire. For India, the most relevant SpaceX product remains stuck in regulatory limbo.
news.image_caption: A rocket launches into the sky, capturing the scale of modern spaceflight
news.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant portion of SpaceX's workforce, and Starlink could transform rural connectivity in India — if regulators ever approve it.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Every Chief Minister Showed Up to NITI Aayog for the First Time. Modi Wants GDP Data Down to the District.
news.excerpt: The 11th Governing Council meeting ended a years-long streak of opposition boycotts and put district-level economic measurement at the centre of India's 2047 development push.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Modi chairing a NITI Aayog Governing Council meeting in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: NITI Aayog's cooperative federalism push shapes where India channels foreign investment, manufacturing capacity and trade-deal benefits — decisions that directly determine which states become viable destinations for NRI capital and reverse-migration.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Sports Ministry Has Sent a 'Sports Passport' Proposal to the PM's Office. For Diaspora Athletes, It Changes Everything.
nri-world.excerpt: If approved, the framework could let PIO and OCI athletes represent India in international competition without surrendering foreign citizenship — a first in Indian sports history, and a potential game-changer ahead of the 2036 Olympics bid.
nri-world.image_caption: India's national football team in action during the 2018 SAFF Championship
nri-world.nri_angle: Millions of Indian-origin athletes who grew up playing football, tennis, and basketball in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia have been legally barred from representing India. The Sports Passport proposal directly addresses the diaspora's exclusion from Indian national teams.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Decades at MIT Press, and Now She Runs Columbia's. Meet Gita Manaktala.
nri-world.excerpt: Columbia University has appointed the Indian American publishing leader as Executive Director of one of the nation's oldest and most respected university presses — a quiet milestone in a field where South Asian representation at the top remains rare.
nri-world.image_caption: Columbia University's Morningside Heights campus in New York City
nri-world.nri_angle: Manaktala's appointment adds to the growing but still thin ranks of Indian Americans leading major American academic and cultural institutions — a quieter form of diaspora achievement than tech CEO headlines, but one that shapes what knowledge gets published, who gets heard, and which ideas reach global audiences.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Bay Area Hindu Temples Hit in Weeks. All Five Indian-American Lawmakers Just Demanded Answers.
nri-world.excerpt: In an unprecedented move, every Indian-American member of Congress has written jointly to the DOJ after a wave of pro-Khalistan vandalism struck temples from Hayward to Newark. The State Department and India's foreign minister have also weighed in.
nri-world.image_caption: A Hindu temple in California, representative of the community institutions being targeted
nri-world.nri_angle: Hindu temples in the Bay Area — the heart of the Indian-American tech community — are being systematically targeted, prompting an unprecedented joint response from all five Indian-American members of Congress.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifty-Six Years After a Prayer at Le Bourget, France Is Getting Its First Traditional Hindu Temple
nri-world.excerpt: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges opens in September with a thirteen-day Festival of Culture — a milestone for Europe's Indian diaspora that began with a 1970 airport layover.
nri-world.image_caption: Carved stone deities at a traditional Hindu temple — the same craft tradition behind the Paris mandir
nri-world.nri_angle: The Paris mandir fills a gap for hundreds of thousands of Indians across Western Europe who have lacked a traditionally built stone temple, and its September inauguration is already drawing NRI families from the US, UK, and Gulf into pilgrimage-tourism packages.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Singapore Just Blocked Fourteen Posts Targeting Its Indian Community. The Content Likely Came from China.
nri-world.excerpt: The city-state invoked its Online Criminal Harms Act to order YouTube, Facebook, and X to disable videos claiming Singapore was being 'overrun by Indians' — a rare, swift use of state power to defend diaspora communities.
nri-world.image_caption: A street in Little India, Singapore, adorned with colourful cultural decorations
nri-world.nri_angle: Singapore's decisive legal intervention to protect its Indian minority offers a sharp contrast to how other countries with large NRI populations have responded to anti-Indian sentiment — and raises questions about what legal tools are available elsewhere.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Seven 'Ratnas' and a 57-Year Legacy: Inside the AIA-NY Annual Benefit Gala 2026
nri-world.excerpt: The oldest Indian-American organisation honoured a xenotransplantation pioneer, a Harvard AI entrepreneur, and five other trailblazers at a packed Flushing gathering — then announced plans for its 39th Deepavali celebration.
nri-world.image_caption: The Association of Indians in America held its annual gala at Terrace on the Park in Flushing, New York
nri-world.nri_angle: Oldest Indian-American organisation (founded 1967) honours new generation of NRI achievers; event bridges generational and professional divides in the community.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Coming Home to Concrete: How the Gulf War Is Fuelling a Kerala Property Rush Among NRIs
nri-world.excerpt: Four months of conflict in West Asia have pushed Gulf-based Keralites to hedge their futures with flats and plots back home — even as construction costs surge 35 per cent and builders struggle to keep up.
nri-world.image_caption: New residential developments in Kochi, Kerala, where NRI property demand has surged amid the West Asia conflict
nri-world.nri_angle: Gulf-based Keralite NRIs — one of India's largest remittance communities — are reassessing permanent settlement plans; war is accelerating a generational shift from 'earn abroad, retire home' to 'invest now, return sooner.'
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: American India Foundation Raises Record $3.8 Million at 25th Anniversary Gala in New York
nri-world.excerpt: The milestone evening at Cipriani Wall Street honoured Infosys CEO Salil Parekh, retired TD Bank chief Bharat Masrani and BNY — with over $1 million pledged from the floor in a single night
nri-world.image_caption: A gala event hall set for a formal philanthropic dinner
nri-world.nri_angle: AIF's quarter-century record demonstrates the maturing financial muscle of Indian-American philanthropy — channelling diaspora wealth back into education, health and livelihoods across 35 Indian states and union territories.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: UAE Arrests 19 Indian Nationals for Spreading Fake Missile Videos Amid Gulf Tensions
nri-world.excerpt: As the Iran-US conflict enters its fourth month, Dubai authorities crack down on misinformation — and the diaspora's largest Gulf community finds itself caught in the crossfire
nri-world.image_caption: The Dubai skyline — home to the UAE's largest concentration of Indian expatriates
nri-world.nri_angle: With 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the single largest expatriate community in any Gulf state — the arrests are a sharp reminder of how wartime information laws can ensnare diaspora workers unfamiliar with local legal thresholds.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Origin Teen Gurnoor Kaur Wins Canada's National Data Science Contest With AI Wheat-Disease Model
nri-world.excerpt: The Grade 11 student from Ontario built a predictive system that forecasts climate-driven crop pathogen outbreaks — and took home a $1,200 Scale AI prize
nri-world.image_caption: A golden wheat field — the crop at the centre of Kaur's AI disease-prediction model
nri-world.nri_angle: Kaur's win adds to a growing roster of Indian-origin students excelling in North American STEM competitions — part of a second-generation pattern where children of immigrants leverage parental emphasis on education into nationally recognised research.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: 'Let Me Cook and Feed People': An Indian Woman's Response to Belfast's Anti-Immigrant Violence
nri-world.excerpt: As masked mobs torched homes in Northern Ireland, Ruchira Rangaprasad rallied 30 strangers to deliver food to terrified families
nri-world.image_caption: Volunteers distributing packaged food at a community relief drive

nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Wait Gets Longer: EB-2 India Retrogression Rattles Thousands of NRI Professionals

markets-finance.title: India Braces for a Wider Fiscal Deficit as Iran War Costs Mount and the Fed Signals No Relief
